LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.BlockChannelCode: A length-n block channel code with M messages consists of an encoder from the message set to length-n input words and a decoder from length-n output words back to the message set.
The encoder of a block code is the function assigning each message its length-n input word.
The decoder of a block code is the function assigning a message estimate to each length-n output word.

Choose a uniform message among M ≥ 1 messages, encode it, and send its codeword through n independent uses of a channel W with finite output alphabet. This gives the joint law of the message and received word.

Choose a uniform message among M ≥ 1 messages, encode it, and transmit its codeword through n independent uses of a channel W with finite output alphabet. This gives the joint law of the message, transmitted word and received word.

Draw a message m uniformly from M ≥ 1 messages, transmit its codeword through n memoryless uses of a channel W with finite output alphabet, and decode the received word Y. The average error is Pr[decoder(Y) ≠ m] under this experiment.

For M ≥ 1 equiprobable messages on a channel with finite output alphabet, the joint probability of message m and received word y is (1/M) times the probability that the n-use memoryless channel produces y from the codeword for m.
For a channel with finite output alphabet and M ≥ 1 equiprobable messages, the message marginal of the joint message–output law is uniform on the M messages.
For M ≥ 1 equiprobable messages on a channel with finite output alphabet, the message–input marginal of the joint message–input–output law is the law of (m,encoder(m)) for a uniform message m.
For M ≥ 1 equiprobable messages on a channel with finite output alphabet, the input-word marginal of the message–input–output law is the pushforward of the uniform message law by the encoder.

For M ≥ 1 equiprobable messages on a channel with finite output alphabet, the input–output marginal of the message–input–output law is obtained by encoding a uniform message and passing its codeword through the n-use memoryless channel.
For M ≥ 1 equiprobable messages on a channel with finite output alphabet, projecting the joint message–input–output law to its message and output coordinates gives the joint message–output law.
For a channel with finite output alphabet and M ≥ 1 equiprobable messages, the message marginal of the message–input–output law is uniform on the M messages.

For M ≥ 1 equiprobable messages on a channel with finite output alphabet, the output marginal of the message–input–output law is the law obtained by encoding a uniform message and sending its codeword through the memoryless channel.

For a code with M ≥ 1 equiprobable messages on a channel with finite output alphabet, the average error equals the decoding error computed from the message and output coordinates of the joint message–input–output law.

For M ≥ 1 equiprobable messages on a channel with finite output alphabet, the average error is the probability, under the joint message–input–output law, that the decoder returns a message different from the one sent.

For M ≥ 1 equiprobable messages on a channel with finite output alphabet, the average error is (1/M)∑ₘ∑ᵧ Wⁿ(y|encoder(m)), where the inner sum runs over output words y decoded to a message other than m.
For a channel with finite output alphabet, the average error probability of a block code with at least one message is nonnegative.
For a channel with finite output alphabet, the average error probability of a block code with at least one message is at most one.
At every blocklength, a code with one message has zero decoding error on any channel with a finite output alphabet. The input alphabet may be infinite.
On a channel with finite output alphabet, a length-zero code with M ≥ 1 equiprobable messages has error probability 1 − 1/M.

For a length-one code with M ≥ 1 equiprobable messages and a finite output alphabet, the joint law of the message m and the single received symbol is the channel joint law with conditional output distribution W(·|encoder(m)₀).

For a length-one code with M ≥ 1 equiprobable messages and a finite output alphabet, the error probability is the average over messages m of the sum of W(b|encoder(m)₀) over symbols b whose one-symbol output word decodes incorrectly.
